image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a fossilized Triceratops skull mounted on a display stand. The image focuses on the cranial structure, highlighting the large eye socket (orbit), the base of a brow horn, and the complex fenestration of the frill. The texture is rough, porous, and mineralized, characteristic of fossilized bone. The background is blurred, suggesting a museum setting.

While the base of one brow horn is visible, the full length of the horns and the nasal horn are outside the frame or obscured by the angle. checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a fossil skull; no skin, scales, or soft tissue are present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
